clue.text: Small terrier, sort of cross

definitions.meaning: a small white long-haired toy dog breed from Malta
the eight-pointed cross of the Knights of Malta

explanation.surface: A little dog of mixed breed, or perhaps just a bit grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' tempts as 'angry' or 'hybrid' to go with the dog, but it is the heraldic cross named after the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the toy dog breed and the eight-pointed cross are named after the island of Malta.

clue.text: It's held to amplify information given to auditors

definitions.text: It's held to amplify information given to auditors

parts.words: It's held to amplify information given to auditors
parts.note: read as accountancy, but auditors are listeners: a handheld device that makes announcements louder for a crowd

explanation.surface: A financial device supposedly expands the figures shown to the accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants; here it means hearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-shaped handheld device makes a speaker's voice louder for those listening.

clue.text: A long time in business, like the principal shareholder?

indicators.note: in places the long time inside the business word

parts.note: a line is a line of business or trade
an eon is an immeasurably long time

explanation.surface: A veteran company man is compared to the main investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lion's share' is the biggest portion, so its holder is lion-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The biggest portion is the lion's share, so whoever holds it is lion-like.

clue.text: For each article, put in odd notes in unnatural language

indicators.note: put in means the first pieces are inserted into the rearranged word
odd means strange or irregular, so these letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Each item has strange musical notes inserted in an artificial tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges the musical notes into ESNTO, and 'put in' places the rest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This invented international auxiliary language was devised by Zamenhof, so it is artificial rather than natural.

clue.text: Language used by Alexander Selkirk

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by the castaway who inspired Robinson Crusoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Selkirk was a Scot, so a Gaelic tongue fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Walker lacking footwear, in the main

definitions.text: Walker lacking footwear, in the main

parts.words: Walker lacking footwear, in the main
parts.note: read as someone mostly barefoot, but 'the main' is the sea, so this is a barefoot person wading at the water's edge

explanation.surface: A hiker who, for the most part, goes without boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly'; it is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wades barefoot in shallow seawater is said to splash about in the shallows.

clue.text: Head supporting right to secure half-day

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the outer pieces enclose the half-day

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
Tories are the political right in Britain
half of Monday, the first three letters

explanation.surface: A chief backs his right to have a morning off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-day' is the first half of Monday. 'Head' looks like a boss but is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A high point of land jutting into the sea is also called a headland.

clue.text: Dismissive command to boxer still in hiding?

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
go! is a command sending someone away

explanation.surface: Telling a fighter to clear off while he is still concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a pugilist; it is the dog breed. To 'lie doggo' is British slang for staying hidden and still.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo means to keep quiet and motionless, avoiding notice.

clue.text: Change of heart for one spotted making tight garment

indicators.note: a change of heart alters the central letter of the word, its heart

parts.note: a leopard is a spotted cat

explanation.surface: A big cat that changes its mind ends up in skintight clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter P of LEOPARD becomes T. 'Change of heart' reads as a mind-change, but the heart is the central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Piping covered with grasses

definitions.meaning: a thin, high-pitched voice is piping

explanation.surface: Pipes laid under the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin, high voice is described by the sound of a reed instrument; marshy ground thick with reeds is likewise.

clue.text: Direction abandoned by mature pop musicians

indicators.note: something abandoned by a word is dropped out of it, so the direction leaves the verb for maturing

parts.note: to mature is to grow up
W is the compass direction west

explanation.surface: A pop band, now older, has lost its sense of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of pop musicians playing together is called by this collective term.

clue.text: Gallico's bird soon goes west for a change

indicators.note: doing something for a change means doing it differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novelist's bird flies off westward for a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Gallico wrote the novella about this bird. 'Goes west' tempts as dying; here 'west' simply gives W to the anagram of SOON GOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Gallico's best-known novella is named after this white Arctic waterfowl.

clue.text: Pope's opening lines about city's religious house

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the city, which sits between them
a word's opening is its first letter, here taken from Pope's

parts.note: RY, short for railway, stands for lines in crosswords
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, is often just Rio

explanation.surface: The beginning of a poem by Alexander Pope concerns an urban church building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pope's opening lines' reads as the start of a poem by Alexander Pope; 'lines' is railway lines, and 'about' wraps the pieces round the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery or convent governed by a prior or prioress is a kind of religious community building.

clue.text: Unpaid, and not at home in ancient surroundings

indicators.note: being at home in somewhere means sitting comfortably inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: hoary means very old, and here it forms the wrapper round the other piece
nor means and not

explanation.surface: An unpaid volunteer feels uncomfortable among antiquities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at home' tempts as OUT or away; instead 'and not' is the piece placed inside, giving the American-style spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: An honorary post is held without salary, as a mark of esteem.

clue.text: Berthed, having crossed part of river like a lake

indicators.note: having crossed means having something across it, so the berthing word holds the river part

parts.note: a boat that has berthed has landed
a lock is a section of river with gates for raising boats

explanation.surface: A boat moored after passing through a lock on a river, like one on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossed' suggests travelling over; it means the river part is held across LANDED.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is enclosed by land on all sides, with no sea coast.

clue.text: A huge quantity that may have to be tacked on

definitions.text: A huge quantity that may have to be tacked on

parts.words: A huge quantity that may have to be tacked on
parts.note: read as something stuck on as an extra, but tacking is a sailing manoeuvre, and a vast expanse of sea is crossed by zigzagging into the wind

explanation.surface: A great amount that might need adding at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacked on' looks like 'appended'; it means sailed on by tacking against the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast body of salt water is crossed by sailing ships, and 'oceans of' means a great deal.

clue.text: Hint given in a poem's the exact opposite

indicators.note: the hint is given in, that is put inside, the other pieces

parts.note: an is the form of a before a vowel
an ode is a lyric poem; ode's gives ODES
a tip is a hint

explanation.surface: A suggestion in verse turns out to say quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given in' puts the hint inside 'a poem's', after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Places diametrically across the globe from each other, and by extension anything directly contrary, are antipodes.

clue.text: Note name held by variety of Alpine plant

indicators.note: held by means placed inside the rearranged word
a variety of something is a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A label naming a particular alpine flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety of' rearranges ALPINE into PENIAL, and 'held by' places the note and name inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that lives for several years, flowering season after season, is described as long-lived in this way.

clue.text: Retailer in northern town knowing about publicity

parts.note: Sale is a town near Manchester in the north of England

indicators.note: about means the knowing word goes round the publicity

parts.note: sly means knowing or cunning
an ad, advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper in a northern town who understands advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sells goods in a shop is a retailer of a kind.

clue.text: Decorate clothing of bride more elaborately

indicators.note: done elaborately means worked over in an intricate way, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A bride's dress is ornamented even more lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is a link word; BRIDE MORE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To stitch ornamental designs on fabric or garments is to decorate them with needlework.

clue.text: Club employee's dishonoured cheque

definitions.meaning: a doorman who removes troublemakers from a nightclub; 's here is 'is'
a cheque that is returned unpaid

explanation.surface: A nightclub worker's cheque has been refused by the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorman ejects unruly guests, and a cheque returned unpaid comes back like a ball.

clue.text: Bishop breaking up dance is dissenter

indicators.note: the bishop breaks up the dance word by sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman who halts the dancing is a nonconformist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking up' looks like an anagram signal, but B simply splits REEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is one who resists or defies authority, as a dissenter does.

clue.text: Increase one dimension of passage through mountain

indicators.note: the passage runs through the mountain, inside it

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for mountain, as in Ben Nevis
a road is a passage or way

explanation.surface: Widening a tunnel through a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to increase width, one of an object's dimensions.

clue.text: Close friend docked to guard old Scottish vessel

indicators.note: to guard means to surround, so the shortened friend goes round the other piece
docked means having its tail cut off, so the friend loses its last letter

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
auld is the Scots word for old

explanation.surface: A good mate, moored in harbour, keeps watch over an ancient Scottish ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' and 'vessel' paint a harbour, but 'docked' cuts the friend's tail and the vessel is a witch's cooking pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal cooking pot, as used by witches, is a vessel.

clue.text: Reportedly captures a small wood

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word heard in speech

parts.note: cops means catches or captures

explanation.surface: News says someone has caught a little woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket of small trees grown for cutting is a small wood.

clue.text: Longing for description of Orsino's musicians' fall

definitions.meaning: ... for something means longing for it
in Twelfth Night Orsino says of the music 'it had a ... fall', a cadence fading away

explanation.surface: Yearning for the cadence Orsino's players gave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link word. Orsino opens Twelfth Night with 'That strain again! It had a dying fall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being desperate for something is being eager to the point of death; Orsino calls the music's fading cadence this.

clue.text: They are known by experts as specimens of Allium cepa

definitions.text: They are known by experts as specimens of Allium cepa

parts.words: They are known by experts as specimens of Allium cepa
parts.note: a botanical description of a common vegetable, with a nod to the idiom that an expert 'knows their' vegetables of this kind

explanation.surface: Botanists recognise these as samples of a particular plant species.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'know your onions' is a British idiom for being expert in something; Allium cepa is the botanical name.
explanation.definitionFit: Allium cepa is the Latin botanical name for the common bulb vegetable used in cooking.

clue.text: Town set-up providing food

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means turned upwards, reading the word backwards

parts.note: a burg is a town

explanation.surface: A town arrangement that supplies meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal slang for something to eat.

clue.text: Tool stealer, they say, who goes outside to scoff?

indicators.note: they say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a pick is a tool and a nicker is a thief, so pick-nicker is a tool stealer

explanation.surface: Someone who pinches tools, rumour has it, is now heading out to sneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' tempts as 'mock'; it is British slang for eating greedily. 'Nicker' is British slang for a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eating an outdoor meal on a rug is having food in the open air.

clue.text: Girl succeeding in a republic

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the girl follows the first word

parts.note: taken as written
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A young woman makes good in a republican state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' looks like 'prospering'; it means following.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Asian country has been a federal republic since 1950.

clue.text: Fashion, finally, makes us very angry

indicators.note: the final word makes a home for the other, read loosely as taking the fashion into itself

parts.note: in the end means finally, giving END
a rage is a craze or fashion, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: In the end, the dictates of fashion leave us furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes us' is a loose containment signal: the word for finally takes the fashion into itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is furious, beside themselves with temper, is extremely angry.

clue.text: Lad eating solitary humbug

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the lad surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a lad is a boy
lone means solitary

explanation.surface: A boy munches a single striped mint sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is also a British boiled mint sweet, which suits 'eating'; here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense or pretentious talk is humbug, a sense shared with baloney.
